blockers: cost model for peak seasonal spikes
notes: Summary: CopperKite runs a mid-size ecommerce platform (multi-market). Primary goal = reduce agent AHT and automate low-risk refunds while keeping full auditability; migrate from manual Zendesk workflows to programmatic tool-calls.

Use-case details: agent-facing assist + one-click actions. Live transcript summarization -> create/update Zendesk tickets via API -> optionally kick off refund flow in payment gateway. Must support: idempotency, detailed audit logs, 2-step refunds (authorize then capture/void).

Traffic profile: normal day ~1200 support sessions/day; peak (promo/holiday) ~8-12x. Concern: model & tooling must remain reliable under spike; want autoscaling + graceful fallback to smaller models or read-only summaries when write paths restricted.

Latency/throughput targets: 95th pct turn-around for agent assist <350ms token latency for routing decisions; ticket create/update path acceptable up to 1.5s end-to-end including middleware. Concurrent agents during peak ~350+.

Model preferences: open models ok for summaries, but legal wants PII redaction step before external model calls for refunds/ticket creation. Interested in Redwood catalog recommendations (quantized variants) + routing policies to keep cost bounded.

Security/compliance notes: PCI considerations for refunds flow (want clear scope). EU customers require data residency for transcripts. Must have SSO/SAML, SOC2 attestation, KMS integration for keys, immutable audit logs for tool actions.

Technical constraints: Zendesk rate limits currently 10 req/s per account; want built-in retry/backoff and automatic batching for ticket patch/update calls. Need idempotency keys emitted by Redwood tool-calls to avoid duplicate refunds.
Quote from VP Support (A. Granger): "If the model suggests refund, the agent must see confidence + linked transaction id, and refunds must go through our two-person approval if above $200."
Procurement hints: legal needs redlined DPA + PCI addendum. Security team sent questionnaire; waiting on Redwood security FAQ answers (see drive link).

POC plan: 2-week pilot with 20 agents; objectives: 1) accurate ticket summarization (f1 > 0.85 on internal evals), 2) successful tool-calls for create/update with zero duplicate refunds, 3) stable latency under synthetic 5x spike. Canary to Dedicated if POC passes.
Emails/meetings: intro demo 2026-02-25 (Leo). Deep-dive security call 2026-03-04 (Priya + Security). POC kickoff targeted 2026-03-15 pending legal signoff.

Integration notes: backend stack = Node.js microservices + middleware queue (BullMQ). Prefer webhook acknowledgements and guaranteed delivery semantics; want tracing hooks in Redwood Console for per-request cost/latency and retriable failure reasons.

Observability ask: per-route token cost breakdown, ticket-level latency trace, and an event stream for all tool-calls to feed internal audit and fraud detection. Alerts on failed idempotent operations >0.1%.

Decision criteria: security signoff (must have KMS + audit logs), POC metrics meet accuracy & latency goals, clear rollback/fallback paths for peak. Price sensitivity around peak unit-costs; prefer Dedicated for predictable peak pricing.
Next steps (short): 1) share redlined DPA by 2026-03-11 (CopperKite legal), 2) Redwood to provide PCI scoping notes and sample audit log export, 3) schedule POC kickoff once legal clears.
